fit: 50:50 corn and soybean comparator in COPD with depression estimates
assessment: The adjusted contrasts versus comparator have opposite signs across active arms and intervals spanning zero. A named blend supplies no independent corn oil or Parkinson depression estimate.

fit: NUTRIMAL mixed oil control and exploratory gait speed
assessment: Neither postintervention gait-speed contrast resolves direction, and the control and protein-only drinks both contain high-oleic sunflower and corn oil. Gait speed does not identify stride length.

fit: COPD blend includes corn oil and protocol measures gait speed
assessment: The supplement establishes the 50:50 blend while the abstract names four-metre gait testing. Accessible source material has no arm-specific gait estimates or stride data.

fit: Injected shared olive oil vehicle in rat liver injury
assessment: The full seven-group report has three injected oil control groups and four injury groups receiving injected vehicle with toxicant. FEBS poster scope and cohort overlap are uncertain. No anxiety or oral cold-pressed comparator.

fit: Injected olive oil vehicle and renal injury
assessment: The renal abstract identifies the vehicle, separate outcome and plant-extract intervention. Shared animals with the liver report are not confirmed. There is no relevant anxiety measure.

fit: Male rat toxicant and vitamin E controls with a corn oil solvent
assessment: The full paper adds a fifth arm and extra tissues. The two reports might share data. The route, carrier use and measured biochemical outcomes cannot establish a culinary or clinical falls effect.

fit: Female rat strain toxicant comparisons with possible shared animals
assessment: The 2016 paper confirms corn oil vehicle and liver/kidney measures. The 2012 author abstract reports different tissues and no vehicle detail. No measured fall or oral corn oil comparison.

fit: Mixed sunflower and corn oil and functional mobility in older adults
assessment: The primary paper shows imprecise gait and balance contrasts in a different population, without reported fall frequency. Individual-response and oxylipin companion papers describe subsets or analyses from the same family.

fit: Mixed soybean and corn oral control with gait and balance proxies
assessment: The official supplement confirms the blend. The study tested physical function in COPD and the accessible materials give no recurrent falls comparison.

fit: Scoping review points to already assessed ginger-tablet MS trial
assessment: The publisher references identify the same Foshati trial studied previously. It is not independent corroboration and supplies no new Parkinson or fresh grated ginger result.
